asserts: Godot 4 requires .NET native DLLs to be copied into the Godot Editor's install directory for them to work correctly within the Editor.
scope: This requirement applies specifically to Godot 4.x releases and contrasts with the behavior observed in Godot 3.5.

asserts: Godot 4.x does not detect controller connection events in Gaming Mode.
scope: When running Godot games on Steam Deck with controllers connected via Bluetooth.
evidence_excerpt:
From the logs players have sent me I can see that:

- controllers connected while the game starts up are detected (via `Input.get_connected_joypads`)
- controller disconnection events are detected
- no controller connection events are detected

asserts: Godot 4.x does not detect controller reconnection events when launched from the Steam client.

The only way to seem to get the the export to take the new dotnet builds is to delete the dotnet build outputs in the mono module.

Fortunately a bash script can take care of cleaning this for us since ``dotnet clean`` does not seem to work and the ``--push-nupkgs-local`` arg as described here also doesn't seem to work: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/contributing/development/compiling/compiling_with_dotnet.html#nuget-packages

This script will delete all folders ignored by git in the folder passed to it:

set -e

prev_pwd="$PWD"

dir_to_clean="$1"
cd "$dir_to_clean"
echo "cleaning directory: $dir_to_clean"
files_to_remove="$(git status . --ignored --short)"

if [[ "$files_to_remove" == "" ]]\ …

# Explanation of commands:
#
# Lists all the files and folders that are being ignored due .gitignore
# git status --ignored --short
#
# Removes the !! that ``git status --ignored --short`` outputs.
# NOTE: This could be an issue if we ever name a file or folder with !
# sed 's/!//g'
#
# Replaces all newline charactes with a ' ' so ``git status --ignored --short`` is space delimited
# tr '\n' ' '
#
# Removes all of the files and folders returned after formatting the output
# rm -rf
#
rm -rf $(echo "${files_to_remove[@]}" | sed 's/!//g' | tr '\n' ' ')

cd "$prev_pwd"

asserts: When exporting a Godot mono project from source, manually deleting the dotnet build outputs in the mono module is necessary to ensure updated builds are used.
scope: The process of ensuring updated dotnet builds are used when exporting a Godot mono project from source.
evidence_excerpt:
I have narrowed it down to the fact that the console executable will create a job object which ensures it waits for not just Godot_v4.5-beta6_mono_win64.exe but all child processes too. … This keeps the godot console waiting on the job object.

On subsequent attempts this will not reproduce if the dotnet server is already running but I can consistently reproduce it by ensuring all "dotnet" processes have been terminated first and deleting the .godot folder so that C# code is recompiled again.

There are four possible fixes or workaround that I have found:
* Setting the "UseSharedCompilation" environment variable to "false".
* Setting `<UseSharedCompilation>false</UseSharedCompilation>` inside the .csproj file.
* Writing a proxy script to invoke Godot_v4.5-beta6_mono_win64.exe (non-console version) and explicitly waiting on it to complete.
